newsitem.title: USA: US Senate Budget chair sees few budget differences.
newsitem.headline: US Senate Budget chair sees few budget differences.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said Thursday there were still a few differences that needed to be ironed out in a budget deal between the White House and congressional leaders.
But he added that he believed talks had come too far to unravel at this point.
"We've reached a point where there are some differences," the New Mexico Republican said. "Clearly compared to even a few days ago, they are very small in number," he added.
Domenici would not specify what the remaining issues were. He made the comments to reporters outside a meeting between White House negotiators and Republican leaders.
Participants in the meeting included White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Missisippi Republican, and House Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia.
Asked whether the budget deal could unravel at this point, Domenici said while there was always that danger, "I believe we've come too far for that to happen."
